svg.text: Lower blocking voltage gives the best figure of merit (D-FoM).
Four devices: 18 W per leg, the knee of the loss curve
Limits: Tj ≤ 125 °C, VDS ≤ 90 V at 0.5 nH.
n = 4 is the smallest count that passes both.
n = 4: Tj 69 °C, 2.24 W per device, 8 driver channels per leg
1 nH instead of 0.5 nH: 93 V peak, still below the rating

svg.text: Constraints → device, layout, parallel count, dc link, machine → coupled verification
Building block: double-pulse-test board and extracted network
DPT board: four cells, eight EPC2361
Ansys Q3D model of the four cells
75 V, 322 A, four cells, extracted gate loops
High-side vDS peak 93 V < 100 V rating at Rg,on 3.5 Ω
Four parallel high-side gate loops equal within 0.3 %
axis from 60 V; dashed: 90 V target, 100 V rating
16 × 75 V cells let 100 V GaN serve a 1200 V, 300 kW drive
The 100 V class has the lowest D-FoM; EPC2361 is the device.
Four devices per switch: 18 W per leg (99.71 %)
69 °C junction and 83 V peak at 0.5 nH loop inductance.
The extracted gate loop (20.6 nH) sets the margin
3.5 Ω turn-on and −1.9 V off-state bias keep the peak at 93 V.
DPT board: waiting for PCB manufacturing and assembly (JLCPCB).
Double-pulse tests at 75 V up to 322 A: per-cell current sharing, overshoot, Eon/Eoff, gate bump.
Then three load-test legs + PCB busbar: one 75 V three-phase level, continuous and thermal tests.
Optimum N: device class versus component count shifts with SiC, GaN and cooling.
Joint battery–converter–machine design on vehicle energy, mass, cost and reliability.
Stack-position common-mode voltage, bearing currents and insulation across the full stack.
